definitions.explanation: An island with no permanent human residents. Often evokes images of tropical adventures or survival scenarios, and is a popular topic in hypothetical questions and games.

examples.japanese: {無人島|むじんとう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{流|なが}れ{着|つ}いた。
examples.english: I washed up on a deserted island.

examples.japanese: {無人島|むじんとう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦{持|も}っていく→持っていく：27431_motteiku⟧なら⟦{何|なに}→何：00498_nani⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧？
examples.english: If you could bring just one thing to a deserted island, what would it be?
It is said that there are about 6,000 uninhabited islands in Japan.

notes:
USAGE:
A common word in everyday Japanese, frequently appearing in hypothetical questions (「{無人島|むじんとう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦だけ→〜だけ：03093_dake⟧⟦{持|も}っていく→持っていく：27431_motteiku⟧なら？」), TV variety shows, and adventure stories. Japan actually has thousands of uninhabited islands.

FORMS:
⟦{無人|むじん}→無人：13388_mujin⟧ (unmanned, uninhabited) + {島|とう} (island).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無人島|むじんとう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{漂着|ひょうちゃく}→漂着：16933_hyouchaku⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to drift ashore on an uninhabited island)
- {無人島|むじんとう}⟦{生活|せいかつ}→生活：01443_seikatsu⟧ (life on a deserted island)
- {無人島|むじんとう}⟦サバイバル→サバイバル：10953_sabaibaru⟧ (deserted island survival)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{離島|りとう}→離島：14597_ritou⟧: remote island — may or may not be inhabited, emphasizes distance from the mainland
- ⟦{孤島|ことう}→孤島：12240_kotou⟧: isolated island — emphasizes isolation, may be inhabited
